key_insight: BLADE improves failure attribution in LLM multi-agent systems by auditing how information is used at key handoffs, not just tracing where it came from.
engineering_relevance: This gives builders a training-free way to localize responsibility in agent pipelines, making debugging and reliability analysis more interpretable.
method: Compute dependency probabilities to select source-to-decision handoffs for auditing.
Use Jev-based probabilistic judgments to check whether a receiving decision faithfully uses its source under task requirements.
Classify handoffs as error introduction, propagation, or repair, then aggregate these signals into a global diagnosis.
evidence_signal: On 1,228 failed runs across five Who&When and Who&When Pro subsets, BLADE achieved the best or tied-best step accuracy among eight strategies and beat All-at-once by 2.2-11.1 points without reference answers.
watch_item: Because it relies on probabilistic auditing of selected handoffs, performance may depend on dependency estimation quality and the reliability of the Jev judgment interface.
paper_title: BLADE: Auditing Information Use for Failure Attribution in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
